summary_en: This phase 2 study tests FLAG-Ida chemotherapy followed right after reduced-intensity total body irradiation (TBI) and donor stem cell transplant. It is for adults age 60 and older with newly diagnosed adverse-risk acute myeloid leukemia or other high-grade myeloid cancer. Fludarabine, cytarabine and idarubicin are given into a vein, with G-CSF given under the skin, starting on day -9 or -8 and ending before TBI on days -1 and 0, with transplant on day 0 or 1; treatment continues unless the disease progresses or toxicity is unacceptable. The record does not state a primary outcome; it says the study tests safety, side effects and how well the treatment works.
summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 evalúa la quimioterapia FLAG-Ida seguida de inmediato por radioterapia corporal total (TBI) de intensidad reducida y trasplante de células madre de donante. Está dirigido a adultos de 60 años o más con leucemia mieloide aguda de riesgo adverso o con otro cáncer mieloide de alto grado, recién diagnosticado. Fludarabina, citarabina e idarubicina se administran por vena, y el G-CSF se administra debajo de la piel, desde el día -9 u -8 hasta antes de la TBI en los días -1 y 0, con el trasplante el día 0 o 1; el tratamiento continúa salvo que la enfermedad progrese o la toxicidad sea inaceptable. El registro no indica un desenlace principal; señala que el estudio evalúa la seguridad, los efectos secundarios y qué tan bien funciona el tratamiento.
who_for: Age 60 or older; adults under 60 may qualify if judged unsuitable for myeloablative conditioning
Newly diagnosed, untreated high-risk myeloid neoplasm, such as adverse-risk AML or high-risk MDS or CMML
Interest in pursuing allogeneic stem cell transplant
Karnofsky score of 70 or higher, or ECOG performance status 0 to 2
not_for: Decompensated heart failure, uncontrolled arrhythmia, or cardiac history precluding transplant
Significant lung disease or symptoms precluding transplant
Treatment with another approved or investigational anti-leukemia agent at study start
